rationale: M49 #754 (CONV-SW-1). LIVE PROBE pre-fix: `class Store { var count = 0; func bare() -> Int { return count }; func dotted() -> Int { return self.count } }` emitted uses(dotted->count) and NOTHING for the bare read — the analyzer's only Uses emission was the self-rooted navigation helper, so every plain identifier read of a declared member was invisible while the `self.` form was not. The fix adds a bare-read pass mirroring java #739 / dart #752, and the real corpus lane then exposed two further contracts this fixture pins. (1) EXTENSION SCOPES: an `extension Foo` carries its name under `user_type`, so the shallow child search left the declaration nameless and every bare read inside every extension was dropped — nio FileType / IPv4Header / EventLoop / ByteBuffer all lost edges this way, and Swift puts a large share of its members in extensions. (2) VALUE SCOPES (CGD15): a `let` bound inside a computed property or a closure is a LOCAL, not a member (nio EventLoop `fullNS`, TestUtils `ipv6Loopback`). Both directions are asserted: expectRelationships catches a dropped branch, forbidRelationships catches a missing gate — the write LHS, the shadowing local, the computed-property local, the implicit member expression (`.fast`, whose base is inferred, not Store) and the argument label (`group:`, which names a parameter, not the member `group`).

expectRelationships.comment: #754: bare read inside an additive expression
#754: second bare read in the same expression
corpus finding: bare read inside an EXTENSION now emits
computed property: bare member read (source falls back to the type)

forbidRelationships.comment: GATE: assignment LHS is a write, never a read
GATE B (CGD15): a local the function binds is not a member read
GATE B: a computed property's `let` is a local, not a member
GATE: `.fast` is an implicit member (inferred base), not a read of Store.fast
GATE: `group:` is an argument label, not a read of the member `group`
GATE A: a local name is not a declared member, so it never emits
